deploy-bot: Promotion attempt to eu-west-1 failed ✅ provenance check failed for image redwood/runtime:release-2026.02 (sha256:abcd1234efgh...). ECR returned REJECTED_FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH. Logs: https://logs.internal/repro/1799991234
maria: saw this during canary -> prod promotion. Fingerprint differs vs us-east-1. not a networking blip, attestation rejected at ECR API. anyone on infra team?
chris: looking now. can you paste the full digest and attestation id?
maria: digest=sha256:abcd1234efgh5678
  attestation id=att-2026-03-20-1678
  deploy job: PROMOTE_CANARY->GLOBAL (pipeline #4821)
chris: quick check: the build artifact pipeline pushes image to us-east-1 then uses cross-account copy; sometimes manifest list gets rewritten by the copy job. suspicion: cross-region replication altered manifest ordering -> verification fingerprint mismatch.
leo: if manifest list reordered, attestation should still match digest unless the copy changed layers. did the copy use --preserve-digest?
maria: copy uses aws ecr batch-copy (internal wrapper) — it should preserve digests but we had an intermittent error earlier in the step logs: "skipping duplicate layer rewrite".
sre_oncall: tagging question — can we fallback to the us-east-1 image for eu-west traffic temporarily? we have capacity to serve from us-east with slight latency bump if we pin routing.
chris: I'm hesitant to force-override attestation. For regulated customers we can't bypass provenance. Options: 1) re-run copy with strict preserve flags and re-attest, 2) rollback promotion and schedule a controlled retag+republish, 3) pin traffic to us-east as emergency mitigation.
tasha_ops: number 1 sounds best if quick. how long to re-run copy+attest?
chris: depends — copy should be minutes, attestation from provenance system adds ~2-3m. but we need to re-run full promote job to ensure no race. estimate 10-15m if nothing else queued.
release_bot: NOTE: holding global release window until provenance passes. Release-note update required: mark delay and mention cross-region publishing investigation.
maria: ok let's do plan A: abort current promotion job, enqueue a manual cross-region copy with strict flags, then re-run attestation. if attestation passes, re-promote. if fails again, fallback to plan C (pin to us-east) and open postmortem. cc @chris @leo @sre_oncall
chris: ack. I'll start manual copy now and watch logs. command I'm running: ```
aws ecr replicate-image --source-region us-east-1 --target-region eu-west-1 --repository redwood/runtime --image-digest sha256:abcd1234efgh5678 --preserve-digest --force-overwrite=false
```
leo: I'll tail attestation service and watch for att-2026-03-20-1678. if it reappears as rejected I'll grab the layers and diff the manifests.
tasha_ops: if re-copy succeeds, remember to update release notes and the changelog entry to include the new digest so external compliance teams can match.
sre_oncall: also flag any customers on strict attestation whitelists so CS can preemptively notify.
chris: good call. if anything blocks beyond 30 minutes we'll cut traffic pin to us-east and open a helix incident (P1 candidate).
maria: manual copy started. progress: uploaded 3/5 blobs (1799991254).
chris: attestation re-run returned PASSED for att-2026-03-20-1678 at 1799991283. re-promote job queued.
release_bot: Promotion resumed by @chris. Canary->Global job #4821 resumed.
maria: canary checks green, no error traces. holding for 10m for rollout window then finalize.
leo: post-action: create a small test that runs cross-region copy and verifies attestation digest equality in CI. ticket filed: #INFRA-4923.
maria: thanks everyone. closing this thread after finalizing release notes and adding a short blameless postmortem. :thumbsup:
